name: William Joyce
role: British fascist organizer and Nazi wartime broadcaster
summary: Joyce founded the National Socialist League and advocated authoritarian leadership, occupational representation and state direction of the British economy. His politics centered on racial nationalism and antisemitism. During the Second World War he broadcast Nazi propaganda from Germany to Britain.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Chapter V demands first-class British armaments to defend Britain and its empire and denounces disarmament.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Chapter III places the issue of currency and the direction of credit under public control and keeps banks subject to state regulation.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Chapter III makes managed currency and higher wages permanent instruments of his economic programme.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: In his April 1, 1945 broadcast, transcript 219, Joyce endorses organized German resistance to advancing Allied occupation.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Chapter III calls for using mechanization to shorten the working day, share employment and maintain higher wages through increased output.

capital-controls.rationale: Chapter III calls for an end to British overseas loans and investment and reserves British credit for domestic and imperial purposes.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Chapter III puts responsibility for the supply of money and its relation to production and prices in the hands of the government.

central-planning.rationale: In chapter V of the book Joyce argues that totalitarian direction of production and purchasing power can meet needs frustrated by private restrictions on output. Chapter III of the pamphlet makes coordinated regulation the alternative to competition.

character-from-environment.rationale: Chapter VI rejects environmental determinism and makes the capacity of human will to overcome material circumstances central to his philosophy.

class-collaboration.rationale: Chapter II of the pamphlet puts employers and employees on equal terms inside the same guilds. Chapter IX of the book describes eliminating class war as a feature of the totalitarian state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Chapters I and VI reject Marxist accounts of society and oppose explaining historical events principally by material and class conflict.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Chapter IX presents class war as incompatible with what Joyce regarded as genuine totalitarian National Socialism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Chapter VI confines clergy to the spiritual care of their congregations, while chapter II vests governing power in political leaders.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: In his April 30, 1945 broadcast, transcript 226, Joyce defends Germany’s claim to Danzig as a German city and argues that territorial gains can have a racial justification.

consent-of-governed.rationale: In chapter II of the pamphlet Joyce says that leaders must be approved by the people and periodically face their judgment by vote. Chapter IX of the book likewise endorses choosing leaders before they exercise power.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Chapters II and III put employers and employees into legally constituted guilds and make those bodies the instruments of state wage regulation.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: Chapter III defines national wealth in terms of goods, services and the spirit of the people, and stresses production as well as resources from the land.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Joyce worked as a German broadcaster against Britain during the war and tried to recruit British prisoners of war as collaborators.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: Chapters III and IX argue that parliamentary assemblies serve as a facade through which a small financial class exercises power.

democracy-best.rationale: Chapters III and IX portray parliamentary democracy as a cover for financial oligarchy and argue for a totalitarian alternative.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Chapter II gives employers and employees equal representation in the institutions of government, and chapter I rejects the division of the nation into opposing economic classes.

direct-action.rationale: Chapter VI insists that substantial change in Britain must come by legal and constitutional methods, and chapter II requires the people to approve the programme and judge the leadership by vote.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Chapter II retains the existing monarchy and gives the King the appointment of ministers while providing separate popular votes on the policy and leadership.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Chapter II gives women in industry a vote there and creates a separate guild to represent mothers and those responsible for the home, giving that body legal powers over maternal and infant welfare.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In chapter VI Joyce argues that people he classifies by ancestry as Jewish cannot coexist on equal terms with the rest of Western society and calls for their separation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Chapter IX explicitly frames political freedom around how much individual liberty a person should surrender for the common welfare. Chapter V makes working and spending for the nation a duty.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Chapters III and IV propose an economically self-sufficient empire with allocated internal markets, phasing out trade with outside countries.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Chapter V treats Jews as foreigners on racial grounds and makes their right to remain in Britain depend on conditions Joyce does not impose on the population he considers British.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Chapter V of the pamphlet treats British national membership as a matter of ancestry and calls for excluding most Jews by treating them as a foreign people. Chapter VI of the book roots nationalism in ancestry and inherited traditions.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: In chapter VII Joyce argues that autocracy suits India and that parliamentary democracy should not be imposed there.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Chapter III urges the expansion of coal mining and production of oil from British coal as part of his programme.

experts-over-public.rationale: Chapter II gives appointed specialists a permanent advisory chamber in fields where the elected occupational Commons has no jurisdiction.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Chapter V makes attending to Britain's own affairs the rule and rejects involvement in the secondary disputes of other powers, while allowing exceptions for vital interests.

free-trade.rationale: Chapter III argues that unrestricted imports depress British employment and wages and proposes displacing foreign goods with British and imperial production.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: In chapter V Joyce argues that withdrawing from competition for international markets would narrow the grounds for war.

gradual-change.rationale: Chapters III and VI demand an economic revolution and a wholesale reorganization of representation and the economy through constitutional means.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: In chapter I Joyce insists that inherited wealth be justified by service and calls for the state to distinguish between heirs who serve the public and those who live solely on the work of their ancestors.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Chapter VII expressly argues that British-style democratic self-government is unsuitable for India and endorses autocracy there.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Chapter V argues that granting Jews political supremacy in Palestine would be unjust to Palestinian Arabs and proposes settling most Jews elsewhere.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Chapters III and VI expressly reject Marx's labour theory of value, citing goods with no demand and discoveries whose significance is disproportionate to the effort involved.

leader-cult.rationale: In chapter IX Joyce publicly presents Hitler's personality as the expression of the will and feeling of the German nation.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: In chapter IX Joyce endorses Carlyle's argument that people should find work suited to their abilities and may properly be compelled to do it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In chapter III Joyce called for government and occupational guilds to replace competitive allocation with regulated production, prices and wages.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Chapter VI explicitly rejects Marx's economic interpretation of history and argues that collective loyalties and actions cannot be explained by economic circumstances.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: Chapter V rejects British intervention in other countries on humanitarian grounds and reserves military force for cases where Joyce judged British interests to be at stake.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Chapter VI of the book and chapter V of the pamphlet advance the antisemitic conspiracy theory that Jews coordinate across borders to dominate Britain's finance, press and politics.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Chapter III of the pamphlet bases currency on production and goods. Chapter V of the book attacks the gold-based system as a source of private financial power.

more-religion-public.rationale: Chapter II sets aside a place for Christian denominations in the upper chamber that would advise national leaders.

nation-first.rationale: Chapter V limits British force to cases where specifically British interests are involved and subordinates foreign commercial engagement to national self-sufficiency.

national-rebirth.rationale: Chapter I calls for a British national revival that would throw off the existing order, and chapter VI presents National Socialism as a revolutionary political and social reconstruction.

national-self-determination.rationale: Chapter IV of the pamphlet rejects Irish separation and insists on the indivisibility of the empire. Chapter VII of the book defends the empire's continued existence under a different system.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Chapter I presents British National Socialism as a joint rejection of liberal capitalist and Marxist materialism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: In chapter III Joyce gives the state responsibility for managing production and guaranteeing purchasing power, wages and conditions of employment.

one-party-rule.rationale: In chapter II Joyce says the Crown should appoint ministers from National Socialist ranks when voters retain the National Socialist system but reject its leaders.

open-borders.rationale: Chapter V calls for moving much of Britain's Jewish population abroad and leaving permission to remain to the state's discretion.

organic-representation.rationale: Chapter II replaces territorial party representation in the Commons with delegates elected through occupational guilds.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Chapter II confines the Commons to vocational and economic matters and gives the executive independent authority to legislate by Order in Council.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Chapters III and IX describe British parliamentary politicians as maintaining a facade of representation behind which a financial elite pursues its interests.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: In chapter V Joyce explicitly justifies extrajudicial political violence against people he blamed for the war. His 1937 constitutional pledge had addressed the narrower question of how to come to power in Britain.

population-transfer.rationale: Chapter V argues that Britain should arrange for much of its Jewish population to leave and make exceptions conditional on service to the state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Chapter II of the pamphlet links freedom to relief from the fear and insecurity of unemployment. Chapter IX of the book contrasts the practical liberty of the millionaire with that of a coal miner.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In chapter VI Joyce explicitly links the survival of nationalism to inherited traditions. Chapter IX frames the transmission of national culture from one generation to the next as a reason to preserve it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Chapter VI argues that ownership and advertising finance give a narrow group control of what readers can see, rendering formal freedom of expression hollow.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Chapter III calls price controls indispensable if supplies lag behind purchasing power after new currency is issued and makes such controls permanent.

production-for-use.rationale: Chapter V makes producing goods to meet people's needs the overriding principle, taking aim at restrictions on output imposed for private profit.

property-fundamental.rationale: In chapter III Joyce subjected property and enterprise to comprehensive control of production, prices, wages, rents and interest in the public interest.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Chapter III makes wide access to property its first justification and subordinates private enterprise to the welfare of the community.

proportional-representation.rationale: Chapter II expressly abolishes party-based representation and assigns Commons representation to elected delegates of occupational guilds.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: In chapters VII and VIII Joyce defends German intervention on behalf of ethnic Germans in Poland and the Sudetenland.

public-money-creation.rationale: Chapter III gives government responsibility for issuing currency in line with production, using employers as the channel to pay it out.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Joyce treats Jewish origin as a racial classification in chapter V of the pamphlet and calls for excluding most Jews from residence. Chapter VI of the book denounces admitting Jewish refugees as a group.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Chapter III assigns the government and its guilds extensive control over prices, output, pay and credit while retaining private enterprise.

religious-nation.rationale: Chapter V defines national belonging in racial terms and explicitly treats a change of religion as irrelevant to his classification.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Chapters I and VI call explicitly for British National Socialism to overturn the existing political and economic order through legal and constitutional means.

right-to-secede.rationale: Chapter IV demands an indivisible British Empire, rejects recognition of an Irish republic and explicitly reserves measures against Irish secession.

second-chamber.rationale: Chapter II retains an elected Commons and reconstitutes the Lords as a second chamber appointed by the Crown to advise on other fields.

separate-church-state.rationale: Chapter II gives Christian denominations formal representation in the reconstituted upper chamber.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Chapter II calls for abolition of the parliamentary party system and replacement of the hereditary Lords with an appointed chamber, while retaining the Crown.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Chapter II replaces party-based representation with occupational representation, transforms the Lords and gives ministers independent lawmaking authority, while retaining the Crown.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Chapter II makes the workers' unions responsible for electing their delegates to Parliament and gives those delegates an equal share with employers in making economic law.

socialized-markets.rationale: Chapter III makes room for private traders and cooperatives side by side and expressly protects individual enterprise.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Chapter III directs British credit to domestic production and singles out making oil from British coal to meet national needs.

state-harmful.rationale: In chapter IX Joyce argues that a modern industrial society requires a totalitarian state to organize its complex economic and social relationships.

strong-leader.rationale: Chapter II of the pamphlet authorizes ministers to legislate by Order in Council to prevent protracted debate from blocking action. In chapter IX of the book Joyce praises leadership with broad powers to act.

suppress-opposition.rationale: At the end of chapter I Joyce proposes making it a felony to teach political doctrines he regarded as creating national disunity, and chapter II abolishes the parliamentary party system.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Chapter III expressly rejects tariffs as a protective instrument and proposes banning imports of goods that Britain can produce.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Chapter IV explicitly rejects obtaining new imperial territory and argues for developing and integrating the lands already held by the British Empire.

total-state.rationale: Chapter IX defends totalitarian government and describes every member of society as integrated into a single whole directed by an undivided leadership.

traditional-family.rationale: Chapter II treats the home as the basis of much of social conduct and makes bringing up a family a public responsibility worthy of national representation.

unions-good.rationale: Chapter II credits strikes with preventing inhuman working conditions and gives unions the job of representing workers in guilds and Parliament.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Chapters II and III give trade unions representation on equal terms with employers in industrial guilds and put economic policy under the direction of the national government.

widespread-small-property.rationale: In chapter III Joyce makes wide access to private property a condition of its legitimacy and commits the state to preserving small private traders alongside cooperatives.

worker-ownership.rationale: In chapter III Joyce defended private enterprise and said personal ownership gave traders and entrepreneurs an incentive worth preserving.

workers-nation.rationale: Chapters I and III demand that workers and unions organize around national interests and explicitly reject international class solidarity.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Chapter VII attributes colonial poverty and malnutrition in part to financial interests extracting wealth and diverting resources away from development in the colonies.

notes: Reviewed Joyce’s economic and constitutional programmes, his accounts of civil liberties, class and race, his foreign policy and empire chapters, and identified wartime broadcasts. Checked the ecology, technology, culture, globalism and political methods statements against those sources, including passages on natural resources, industrial machinery, propaganda and the means of obtaining power. Joyce did not hold legislative office. A Gutenberg catalogue search returned an unrelated entry.
